meta.title: CZ-6A Launch visibility
notes: Reconstruction (revision 2, 2026-10-24), not telemetry or a unique solution. Liftoff was announced at 18:15 Beijing time (10:15 UTC); seconds-level T0 is not known.

The lower ascent is a 2-D point-mass model with a propulsion surrogate calibrated on the triangulated December 2025 CZ-6A ascent. It is fitted to two untimed ground reports: at N39.00 E110.12 the rocket crossed above the Moon at 1.6x its elevation, and at N37.76 E110.93 the sunlit rising path looked nearly straight. It also fits a ballistic booster range to the NOTAM booster zone. The reports constrain climb geometry, not timing.

The upper-stage surrogate is fitted to the first catalog elements of 2026-240A (assumed payload; identity unconfirmed). The cutoff state is about 3 km from that SGP4 state. The March Yaogan-50 02 reconstruction remains a weak template.

The dogleg is attributed to stage 1 and NOTAM A5283/26 to the booster drop zone. The plane change is still carried by the stage-2 steering surrogate; booster burnout/separation and stage timing are model quantities and are not shown as events.
NOTAM 10:07–10:28 UTC is a hazard-area activation interval, not launch-time limits or an insertion constraint. The 09:30–11:00 UTC selector is an exploratory range, not an announced launch window.
Shifting T0 reuses the same Earth-fixed (ECEF) trajectory and changes the solar geometry; it does not reoptimize dynamics or propagate a newly fitted orbit.

Source positions and velocities use a TEME-like frame with GMST rotation, UTC approximating UT1 and no polar motion. The exporter converts to ECEF and resamples with cubic Hermite interpolation; it does not reoptimize or integrate a new trajectory.
The upper-stage and orbit dynamics include central gravity and J2. Higher harmonics, post-insertion maneuvers, fragmentation and debris descent are not modeled.
Altitude samples are WGS84 geodetic ellipsoidal heights in km. Perigee and apogee are orbital radii minus the WGS84 equatorial radius; these are not the same altitude convention.
Sunlight uses the geometric Sun centre from the shared DE440s ephemeris and WGS84 ellipsoidal Earth occultation. The solar table is linearly interpolated in ECEF at 30-second cadence.

The 10° visibility envelope is sampled during sunlit ascent for sea-level observers with Sun-centre altitude ≤0°, then clipped to the observer night side at the insertion reference epoch. Post-insertion orbit tracks do not enlarge the ascent envelope.
No brightness, atmospheric refraction or extinction, weather, terrain, finite solar-disc emergence, or plume size is modeled. Geometric visibility is not a claim of naked-eye detection.
The 1.5 revolutions shown are exactly 1.5 times the insertion Keplerian period in elapsed time, not a claim of an exact J2 ground-track repeat or true-anomaly recurrence.

The model TLE keeps the label PRELAUNCH MODEL - NOT OBSERVED and placeholder catalog number 00000. It is fitted to the reconstructed numerical orbit and is not the catalog element set; some TLE consumers reject this placeholder.

The rocket drawing drops its four solid boosters at the modeled T+134 s, after burnout at T+88 s, and stage 1 at T+230 s; from insertion only the payload is drawn. These are drawing states taken from model quantities, not timeline events; the fairing jettison time is not modeled, so the fairing is shown until insertion.
about: Reconstruction fitted to ground reports and the first catalog orbit; not telemetry.
